2609.08576.title: Which Forms of Caregiver Feedback Support Grammar Learning? A Reinforcement-Learning Study of Child-Like Language Models
2609.08576.paper_summary: Social interaction is central to children's language learning, but the effects of different forms of caregiver feedback are difficult to isolate in naturalistic data. We use child-like language models as controlled learners to test which forms of feedback support grammatical development. Small GPT-2-style models are pretrained on child-directed language from CHILDES, then fine-tuned with reinforcement learning using reward models trained to capture four feedback types: communicative feedback, structural alignment, semantic contingency, and affective feedback. Reward fine-tuning yields limited gains on minimal-pair evaluations, but clearer effects in free generation. Structural alignment produces the strongest improvements in grammaticality, providing a novel, plausible mechanistic account of how this feedback can support grammar learning. Communicative feedback yields more moderate gains. In contrast, semantic contingency and affective feedback do not improve grammaticality, although further analyses suggest that they may support other aspects of language learning beyond grammar. These results suggest that different forms of caregiver feedback make complementary contributions to language learning.
2609.08576.paper_summary_zh: 社交互動對於兒童的語言學習至關重要，但在自然數據中，很難孤立不同形式的照顧者反饋的效果。<lb/>我們使用類似兒童的語言模型作為受控學習者，以測試哪些形式的反饋支持語法發展。<lb/>小型的 GPT-2 風格模型在 CHILDES 的兒童導向語言上進行預訓練，然後利用強化學習進行微調，使用訓練以捕捉四種反饋類型的獎勵模型：交際反饋、結構對齊、語義偶然性和情感反饋。<lb/>獎勵微調在最小對比評估中產生有限的增益，但在自由生成中效果更為明顯。<lb/>結構對齊在語法性方面產生了最強的改善，提供了一種新穎且合理的機制解釋，說明這種反饋如何支持語法學習。<lb/>交際反饋則帶來了較為適中的增益。<lb/>相反，語義偶然性和情感反饋並未改善語法性，儘管進一步的分析表明它們可能支持語言學習的其他方面，而不僅僅是語法。<lb/>這些結果表明，不同形式的照顧者反饋對語言學習做出了互補的貢獻。
